cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: this context may or may not be relevant to your tasks
cards.claim: Claude Code wraps CLAUDE.md in a reminder saying it may be irrelevant, so the more of it that does not apply to the current task, the likelier the model is to ignore all of it.
cards.evidence_detail: No numbers; quotes the injected system-reminder text as the mechanism.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md trim: explains why a 390-line always-loaded file loses adherence

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Wrap conditionally-relevant sections of the CLAUDE.md in `<important if="condition">` XML tags.
cards.claim: Rewrite CLAUDE.md so domain-specific rules sit in inline <important if="specific trigger"> blocks, giving the model an explicit relevance signal instead of sharding into separate files.
cards.evidence_detail: Technique with a worked before/after example; no measured adherence data.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md restructure: invariants sections (outbox, bill freeze, dispatcher) wrapped by trigger condition

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: if it's relevant to 90%+ of tasks, leave it bare.
cards.claim: Keep project identity, map and tech stack bare at the top; wrap only guidance relevant to specific kinds of work, and keep all commands.
cards.evidence_detail: Rule of thumb, no data.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md: decide which sections stay bare (stack table, where things live, commands) vs conditional

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Frontier models can reliably follow a few hundred. Claude Code's system prompt and tools already use ~50
cards.claim: Instruction budget: a frontier model follows only a few hundred instructions, ~50 already spent by Claude Code itself, so CLAUDE.md should be as lean as possible.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as fact with no source or experiment.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md: a numeric instruction budget to size the trim against

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Cut any instruction that a linter, formatter, or pre-commit hook can enforce
cards.claim: Delete from CLAUDE.md anything a linter/formatter/hook can enforce or the agent can discover from existing code patterns, and suggest pre-push or pre-commit hooks instead.
cards.evidence_detail: Rule list; says LLMs are in-context learners so consistent patterns need no instruction.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md trim; re-opens the skipped pre-commit gate / hooks decision (mark as re-opening)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Cut code snippets. They go stale and bloat the file.
cards.claim: Replace code snippets in CLAUDE.md with file-path references, and delete vague instructions like 'follow best practices' that are not concrete and actionable.
cards.evidence_detail: Rule list, no data.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md: remove inline snippets and vague lines; point to files

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Do not shard into separate files that require the agent to make tool calls to discover
cards.claim: Against progressive disclosure by default: sharding CLAUDE.md into files the agent must fetch is only justified when the extra context is very verbose; inline-but-conditionally-weighted is preferred.
cards.evidence_detail: Design stance; no comparison data.
cards.landing: Knowledge-store pilot: tension with a store the agent must consult by tool call (and W2: consultation is not guaranteed)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Pause, reset, and change approach rather than continuing to thrash.
cards.claim: A conditional-rules skill (Uncle Bob style) tells the agent to say no, surface mistakes early, ask for evidence when debugging, and reset when looping, triggered when the user swears or is upset.
cards.evidence_detail: Tongue-in-cheek 'questionably useful' plugin; no evidence.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious; possible source of honesty/uncertainty lines for the reviewer or closing-message rules

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: implement the single highest priority feature using up to 5 subagents
cards.claim: The Ralph prompt shape: each fresh iteration reads the specs, the code and an IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, implements exactly one top-priority item, with a cap on subagents.
cards.evidence_detail: The prompt file itself; the repo it produced is the evidence (322+ tests, all milestones complete per the plan), no cost or failure rate given.
cards.landing: Phase routine in ship plan §0: one item per fresh context, plan file as the state carrier

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: ensure all tests and linting passes with `bun check && bun test`, then update IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md
cards.claim: Backpressure inside the loop: one combined check command must pass before the plan file is updated and a commit is made, and the plan file is rewritten with progress each iteration.
cards.evidence_detail: Prompt step 2 and 3; no measurements.
cards.landing: Phase routine: single verification command gate before the decisions journal / PR update

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: including anything in the out of scope / future work - that's now in scope!
cards.claim: The prompt declares deferred and out-of-scope plan items in scope so the loop never stalls waiting for a human to promote them.
cards.evidence_detail: One line in the prompt; plan shows a 'Deferred Features (COMPLETE)' phase consumed this way.
cards.landing: Ship plan: how deferred register items are picked up (counter-example to FixFlow's gated phases)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: list open issues and compare with known-issues/
cards.claim: Each iteration begins by syncing GitHub issues into a local known-issues/ folder (as markdown) and folding new ones into the implementation plan, making human feedback an input to the loop.
cards.evidence_detail: Curl/jq commands in the prompt; the plugin variant stores issues as JSON instead.
cards.landing: Phase routine step 0: pull the owner's field defects into the plan before choosing the next item

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: do not include any claude attribution
cards.claim: The loop commits with git add -A and a plain commit message, explicitly without Claude attribution; the plugin variant also pushes to main each iteration.
cards.evidence_detail: Prompt lines 3 and 4 (push only in the plugin repo).
cards.landing: nowhere obvious; contrast with FixFlow's branch-never-main and attribution rules

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: All milestones complete! M1-M4 plus ALL deferred/future features implemented and tested
cards.claim: The plan file doubles as a progress ledger with phases, checkbox items, a Current Status block and a test count (322 tests), which is the only state a fresh iteration needs.
cards.evidence_detail: Plan lists 322 passing tests plus typecheck and lint passing; not independently verified.
cards.landing: Phase routine: a single checkbox plan with a Current Status block as the cold-resume anchor (P1 trial)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: parallel processing of files to significantly speed up builds
cards.claim: The Ralph-built repo produced a very large amount of agent-written documentation (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md about 343 KB, README about 144 KB, many GIT_* research files), showing the loop's output sprawl when no one prunes it.
cards.evidence_detail: File sizes observed locally (343,275 and 143,883 bytes); Dex does not comment on it.
cards.landing: Phase routine: a size cap or prune step on plan/journal files so cold-resume reads stay small

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Turn any MCP server into a CLI for easy use with subagents
cards.claim: MCP servers are wrapped as CLIs so sub-agents can call them through bash, instead of loading MCP tool schemas into context.
cards.evidence_detail: One-line README; no mechanism or numbers given.
cards.landing: Custom agents/skills: tool exposure for sub-agents via a CLI wrapper to keep tool definitions out of context

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: run `mcp__agent-launch` and tell it a new number which is `your_number + 1`
cards.claim: Sub-agent recursion is demonstrated with a counter agent that launches itself through an agent-launch MCP tool up to depth 10, writing a file at each level.
cards.evidence_detail: A toy demo agent definition; the repo's one-line description is 'Sub-agent recursion with Claude Code'; no results shown.
cards.landing: Workflow library: recursive sub-agents as a way around the no-nesting limit of Task

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: YOUR ONLY JOB IS TO DOCUMENT AND EXPLAIN THE CODEBASE AS IT EXISTS TODAY
cards.claim: Read-only research agents are constrained to describe the code as-is (no critique, no root cause, no suggestions) with file:line references, on Sonnet with Read/Grep/Glob/LS tools only.
cards.evidence_detail: Agent definition file; frontmatter sets model: sonnet and a four-tool allow-list.
cards.landing: Custom agents: locator/analyzer agent specs with tool allow-list and model per role (extends fixflow-explorer)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Read these files yourself in the main context before spawning any sub-tasks
cards.claim: The research command has the lead read the mentioned files fully itself, then spawn parallel sub-agents, wait for all, and synthesize, to minimize context usage.
cards.evidence_detail: Command prompt text; no measurements.
cards.landing: Workflow scripts: lead-reads-first then fan-out then synthesize pattern

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: compact and summarize your context without losing any of the key details
cards.claim: A handoff command writes a concise timestamped, ticket-keyed document for a new session (paired with resume_handoff) as a manual compaction.
cards.evidence_detail: Command prompt; filename convention YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS_TICKET_slug.md.
cards.landing: Phase routine closing message / decisions journal as the handoff; cold-resume trial design

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: subagents, and RLM-like orchestration patterns
cards.claim: Fold is an Effect-native agent core whose features include sub-agents and RLM-like (recursive language model) orchestration, intended for building custom coding agents.
cards.evidence_detail: README feature sentence; no benchmarks or description of the orchestration patterns.
cards.landing: Workflow library: recursive/RLM-style orchestration as a saved pattern

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: log-based state, tool support, hook support, subagents and skill facades, event streaming, auto-compaction
cards.claim: fold-core keeps agent state as an append-only event log with built-in auto-compaction (autoCompact: { enabled: true }), hooks, sub-agents and skills.
cards.evidence_detail: Package feature list and a code sample enabling autoCompact; no thresholds or quality data.
cards.landing: Context budget: a log-based session as a way to audit consultation and compaction events (W2: observable record)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Claude gets `write`/`edit`, while GPT/Codex gets `apply_patch`.
cards.claim: The tool set advertised to the model is selected per model on every request, so switching models reselects tools automatically (Claude gets write/edit, Codex models get apply_patch).
cards.evidence_detail: README design note; no measurements.
cards.landing: Effort/model routing: tool formats tuned per model when mixing models across verifiers

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Existing log identity is authoritative.
cards.claim: A resumed session trusts the existing log: a conflicting session id, a nonempty log without valid session history, or multiple session starts fails loudly rather than silently initializing a new session; model/prompt changes on resume are recorded as configuration epochs.
cards.evidence_detail: README design rules for Session.open; no data.
cards.landing: Cold-resume: fail loudly when the resume source is inconsistent; record config changes as dated epochs

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Keep session construction **and use** within the owning scope.
cards.claim: One session owns one log with at most one active handle; reusing a backend across unrelated sessions is wrong because a fresh layer pointing at the same file is still the same persistent log.
cards.evidence_detail: README note on Effect layer memoization; library-specific.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Do not add an npm token to GitHub.
cards.claim: Releases use tag-triggered npm trusted publishing via GitHub OIDC, a Validate Publish dry-run workflow, and a publish script that is safe to rerun after a partial publish (existing versions skipped).
cards.evidence_detail: Release procedure, including the warning not to skip a package based only on a failed publish; confirm in the registry first.
cards.landing: Deploy traps: idempotent resumable release step and 'verify by the registry, not by the error' rule (cf. CLAUDE.md verifying a deploy by content)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: read the source there rather than relying on v3 knowledge or docs.
cards.claim: The AGENTS.md is short and points the agent at the real dependency source checkout (../effect) for the v4 API instead of trusting training-data v3 docs; versions pinned once in a catalog.
cards.evidence_detail: Short repo instruction file; command list plus pointer.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md: a 'when unsure, read X source' pointer pattern; shape of a lean agent file (~30 lines)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: oxlint (with the `@effect/tsgo` recommended preset), then the typed rules in `tools/typed`
cards.claim: Domain mistakes are enforced by custom typed lint rules and patched compiler diagnostics (Effect language service) rather than prose in the agent file.
cards.evidence_detail: Commands section only; implies lint-as-instruction.
cards.landing: Backpressure: encode CLAUDE.md invariants as lint/import rules (FixFlow already has import-linter); candidates for the CLAUDE.md trim

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: tool interfaces kept separate from their executors
cards.claim: agentlayer-core is a resumable agent loop with tool interfaces separated from executors (filesystem, sandboxed just-bash, Yjs CRDT filesystem), so the same tool contract can run against different back ends.
cards.evidence_detail: Package description and dependency diagram; no benchmarks.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious; design principle for verifier tool sandboxes (read-only executors)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: multi-provider coding agent CLI (Anthropic/OpenAI/Codex/Copilot/Fireworks) with RPI-style sub-agent orchestration
cards.claim: The codelayer agent in agentlayer ships RPI-style (research, plan, implement) sub-agent orchestration built into a multi-provider CLI, and docs-agent is a CI agent that updates markdown docs to match source changes on pull requests.
cards.evidence_detail: README table rows; no behaviour detail.
cards.landing: Docs drift: a CI docs-sync agent for CLAUDE.md and prose docs (CLAUDE.md 'Keeping this file honest'); RPI orchestration as saved workflow

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: `bun check` is the preferred way of doing repo verification.
cards.claim: The agent file names one command that runs typecheck, formatter and tests in parallel as the preferred verification step, and lists contributor policy (vouch required for PRs) with a rule to keep templates and workflows aligned with CONTRIBUTING.md.
cards.evidence_detail: CLAUDE.md is ~35 lines; AGENTS.md is a byte-identical copy.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md commands: one aggregate check command; lean file shape; CLAUDE.md = AGENTS.md duplicate pattern

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: external pull requests need a vouch
cards.claim: Contributor gating uses a vouch list: issues open to all except denounced users, PRs only from vouched contributors, enforced by Vouch workflows.
cards.evidence_detail: Policy summary in README.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: It runs a real `claude` session inside tmux, sends a prompt, and emits stream JSON.
cards.claim: Shannon lifecycles a real interactive Claude Code session in tmux and tails its on-disk transcript JSONL, giving a headless claude -p style SDK without ever using claude -p or calling the API directly.
cards.evidence_detail: README architecture diagram; no measurements of why interactive differs from -p.
cards.landing: Workflow orchestration: drive interactive sessions headlessly, and read the transcript JSONL as an audit trail of whether the routine/store was used (W2)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: `@dexh/shannon-agent-sdk` is a Claude Agent SDK-compatible facade
cards.claim: A Claude Agent SDK-compatible facade lets code written against the SDK run on a subscription-backed interactive session instead, with parity still in progress.
cards.evidence_detail: README; parity tracked in GOAL_PROGRESS.md (not in bundle).
cards.landing: Workflow library: SDK-compatible drivers for saved workflows; cost routing

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Follows "read 1500+ lines first" rule to understand context
cards.claim: Role personas (developer, code-reviewer, rebaser, merger, multiplan-manager) are installed as files and chosen via CLAUDE.md, with rules such as read 1500+ lines first, 20+ item TODO lists, commit every 5-10 minutes, and delete more code than you add.
cards.evidence_detail: README bullet summary of persona rules; no results.
cards.landing: Custom agents: reviewer/merger personas as agent files rather than CLAUDE.md prose; existing Opus reviewer role

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: npx multiclaude launch branch-name plan-file.md
cards.claim: A manager persona splits a feature into worker plan files and launches one agent per branch via a launch/cleanup CLI (using Makefile setup and teardown targets), then a merger persona consolidates the branches.
cards.evidence_detail: README usage; repo develops itself with worker plans, no outcome data.
cards.landing: Workflow library: plan-file-per-worker fan-out with worktree setup/teardown and a merger step

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: **DO NOT PROCEED WITHOUT SELECTING A PERSONA.**
cards.claim: The repo's CLAUDE.md uses a mandatory-persona gate in capitals (read one persona file before any work), which is the style the later improve-claude-md skill argues against.
cards.evidence_detail: Template file; no adherence data. Shipped by the promptx tool.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md: counter-example of emphatic gating text; note the later reversal toward conditional blocks

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: At any given point, your input to an LLM in an agent is "here's what's happened so far
cards.claim: Own the context window: build a custom context format (events packed into one message as XML-ish tags, then 'what's the next step?') instead of default role-based messages, to maximize density and attention efficiency.
cards.evidence_detail: Code example and screenshots of a token-count comparison, no benchmark.
cards.landing: Context budget: how subagent prompts and phase handoffs are serialised

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Consider hiding errors and failed calls from context window once they are resolved.
cards.claim: Resolved errors and failed calls should be removed from the context window, and the five benefits of owning it are density, error handling, safety, flexibility and token efficiency.
cards.evidence_detail: Short list; no data.
cards.landing: Context budget: strip resolved failures from handoffs and journals so cold-resume reads stay clean

cards.source_title: 12-factor-agents factor-03 (added section 'Don't take it from me')
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Everything is context engineering.
cards.claim: Dex positions context engineering as the umbrella (prompts, retrieved docs, history, memory, output instructions) and notes the term took off about two months after 12-factor agents, citing Karpathy, Tobi Lutke and a July 2025 cheat sheet.
cards.evidence_detail: Links to third-party tweets as support; no experiment. Added after 2025-06-25 (screenshot date).
cards.landing: nowhere obvious; framing for the knowledge-store design

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you want the flexibility to be able to try EVERYTHING.
cards.claim: Explicit epistemic stance: he does not know the best way to hand context to a model and argues for keeping the structure flexible and experimenting, excluding temperature, fine-tuning and training from scope.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated twice in the factor.
cards.landing: Measurement posture: try-and-measure rather than fixed doctrine (cf. L1 effort routing evidence)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: JSON vs XML for thread history (XML more token-efficient)
cards.claim: Workshop notes record that XML-style thread serialisation was more token-efficient than JSON for the agent's history.
cards.evidence_detail: One bullet in a learnings file; no counts.
cards.landing: Context budget: format of state files and journals that agents re-read

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Debug artifacts - Test runs preserved in ./tmp/test_TIMESTAMP/ directories
cards.claim: The workshop CLAUDE.md is a bullet file of implementation learnings, pitfalls avoided, chapter status with checkmarks and testing commands, including a script that simulates the Colab environment in a clean venv and keeps timestamped debug artifacts per run.
cards.evidence_detail: Agent-maintained notes; shape is learnings + status + commands.
cards.landing: Knowledge store / journal shape: pitfalls-avoided list and per-run preserved artifacts for a test-environment simulation

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: mirrors your pi sessions to HumanLayer, where you can read them in the web app.
cards.claim: The pi extension mirrors every session entry, tool call, compaction summary, task files and a repo diff to a cloud task, giving a reviewable record of what the agent did outside the terminal.
cards.evidence_detail: Product README; alpha. Sends events with fixed ids so resends do not duplicate.
cards.landing: Compliance observability: a session log external to the agent answers 'was the routine/store consulted' (re-opens the skipped measurement pipeline/hooks; mark)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Each prompt adds an `artifacts_directory_information` section to the system prompt.
cards.claim: Each task has a folder of artifacts linked into the repo (git-excluded), named in the system prompt each turn with an instruction to look there first when asked to continue a task, with files written there synced to the task.
cards.evidence_detail: README describing a mechanism, no data.
cards.landing: Cold-resume: a standing hint in context pointing at the task folder as first stop; vs always-loaded CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Calls in one session run one at a time, in order
cards.claim: Tool calls from the comment tools are serialised per session because a reply reopens a thread that a resolve in the same turn closed.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated in the opencode README as a concrete ordering bug rationale.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious; parallels the outbox 'no mutual exclusion on a stable id' known defect in CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: pi runs every tool without asking, so the web app never shows an approval.
cards.claim: The README lists its own limits plainly (no redaction, never-expiring daemon token, crash loses queued items until resume, no approvals in pi, branches flatten), and documents retry/drop policy per HTTP status plus size caps (5000 items or 50 MB, drop oldest events but never status updates).
cards.evidence_detail: Explicit limits section with numbers; retry: network and 408/425/429/502/503/504 forever with backoff 0.5s to 30s, 500 five times then skip, 400/413/422 skip.
cards.landing: Outbox policy and honest-limits sections in docs; compare to FixFlow's syncClassification (retry vs park vs drop by status)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: takes the PAT `hl-pat-mock`
cards.claim: A mock cloud server validates request bodies against copies of the real server contracts (400 on mismatch) and supports scripted failure injection (status, network drop, hang, times), so the real client is tested with no network or model.
cards.evidence_detail: Described mock-cloud commands; tests run the real server half in a fake host.
cards.landing: Verifier tooling: contract-checking fakes with fault injection to test mobile outbox without a live backend

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Subagent sessions show as the Task call in their parent.
cards.claim: Sub-agent sessions are folded into their parent session as a Task call when mirrored, and web replies queue behind a running turn; the stop button interrupts; approvals can be answered in either place.
cards.evidence_detail: README feature list.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious; sub-agent visibility in logs

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: commits `Sync from humanlayer/synclayer@<sha>`
cards.claim: The installable repo is a generated build of source in a private monorepo, committed with the source SHA in the message, so every published state names the plan/source commit it came from.
cards.evidence_detail: Publish script description.
cards.landing: Phase routine: provenance by SHA in commit/PR text (cf. 'Plan @ <sha>')

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: HumanLayer's skills (`@create-research`, `@create-tech-design`, `@show-me` and the rest
cards.claim: The RPI workflow ships as a bundle of named skills (create-research, create-tech-design, show-me, and others) bundled into plugins for two different host agents, with a library_researcher tool, so the workflow is a reusable package rather than per-task prompts.
cards.evidence_detail: Names listed in README; skill contents not in bundle.
cards.landing: Skills library: package phase-routine steps as named skills reusable across hosts

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: claude plugin marketplace add dexhorthy/slopfiles
cards.claim: Skills are distributed as plugins through a git-hosted marketplace installed with two commands, making configuration shareable and versionable.
cards.evidence_detail: Install instructions.
cards.landing: Skills/agents/workflow library: publish saved workflows as a repo plugin

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Read the spec markdown file
cards.claim: A skill that carries a template, an example spec and a build script beside its SKILL.md, converting a markdown spec to HTML slides deterministically with a script for the standalone-file step.
cards.evidence_detail: Skill file structure; no data.
cards.landing: Skills: bundle templates/scripts with a skill (e.g. the owner one-page view generator)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: falls back to seeded fixture data so the UI still renders
cards.claim: The app falls back to seeded fixture data when the live data source has no match, and the seed script uploads only git ls-files entries so .env and ignored files stay local.
cards.evidence_detail: Ordinary setup README; no harness ideas beyond that.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious

gaps: kustomark-ralph-bash README.md (144 KB), IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md (343 KB) and the ~20 other GIT_*/HELP_* files are generated project output; only the head of README and the named PROMPT.md/PARALLEL_BUILDS.md were read.
kustomark-ralph-plugin IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md read only to about 3.5 KB of 9.5 KB.

claudelayer: README is a title only; CLAUDE.md is Bun boilerplate. Only grepped/skimmed the agents (recursive analyzer, counter) and commands (research_codebase, create_handoff); the .mcp.json agent-launch server and src/ were not read, so the recursion mechanism is inferred from counter.md.
agentlayer: CONTRIBUTING.md and MAINTAINERS.md were not in my file list and not read.
fold: GOAL_PROGRESS and shannon GOAL_PROGRESS.md not in bundle. fold publishing.md is operational and carded lightly.

12-factor-agents README only grepped (not read in full); git history to confirm which edits post-date 2025-06-01 was unavailable, so factor-03 dates (2025-06/07) are estimated from the in-text screenshot dates (2025-06-25) and the July 2025 cheat-sheet reference.
multiclaude README gives no date and is not in the inventory; date 2025-06 is a guess. Repo URL assumed under dexhorthy.
Commit dates for fold, agentlayer, pi, opencode, claudelayer, shannon etc. are taken from the inventory, not the files.

new_sources.why: Not in inventory; early persona-based multi-agent workflow with launch/cleanup CLI and merger agent.

new_sources.why: Inventory lists only the repo's description; the RPI command prompts inside are a primary source for the plan/implement/handoff routine.

new_sources.why: Inventory mentions the commits but not the workshop CLAUDE.md learnings or hack/testing.md.
